points.name: 16_PMA
points.title: PMA
points.languageDesc: On 11 September 1918, the construction of the Aeronautical Material Depot (PMA) began, an event which indelibly marked the history and lives of the population of Alverca do Ribatejo. In the early days, the PMA became a pole of stability and employment for men and women, some still adolescents, promoting the retention of the local population and contributing to the growth of the Municipality of Vila Franca de Xira. From 14 February 1928, it became known as General Aeronautical Materiel Workshops (OGMA).

points.name: 01_DGMFA
points.title: DGMFA
points.languageDesc: On 12 September 1924, the founding of Portuguese military's Aeronautical Division created a need for the General Depot of Air Force Materiel (DGMFA) in Alverca do Ribatejo. The DGMFA began to operate independently of the General Aeronautical Materiel Workshops (OGMA), under the command of Major Eduardo Rosário Gonçalves, the first to perform these functions. Currently the DGMFA maintains its mission to receive, store and distribute the materiel of the Portuguese Air Force, always guided by Camões' motto: "E do mais necessário vos proveja" [And stock with needed store each empty hold].

points.name: 02_DOGMA
points.title: DOGMA
points.languageDesc: During the Colonial War, between 1961 and 1974, the OGMA had delegations (known in Portuguese as DOGMA) located in the overseas colonies, where technicians were sent to maintain aircraft of the Portuguese Air Force (FAP) stationed there. DOGMA 2 was located in Luanda, Angola, and DOGMA 3 in Maputo [then Lourenço Marques], Mozambique

points.name: 03_Vistas Aéreas - do PMA às OGMA
points.title: Aerial Views
points.subtitle: from PMA to OGMA
points.languageDesc: The OGMA were created on 14 February 1928 as part of the Portuguese Air Force, following the development of the Aeronautical Materiel Depot (PMA). In March 2005 the company was privatised through the acquisition of a majority stake by Airholding SGPS, S.A., and eventually became OGMA – Indústria Aeronáutica de Portugal, S.A.

points.name: 13_OGMA - Hangar do Balão
points.title: OGMA
points.subtitle: Balloon Hangar
points.languageDesc: Built in 1925 for the maintenance of hydrogen balloons, the OGMA balloon hangar is the only one in the world of its kind today and was actually the only one to have been built in Portugal. At 13.1 metres high and 40 metres long, its unique geodesic architectural construction is covered with 22,800 fibre cement tiles. The internal structure is composed of diagonally-arranged wooden beams, resembling the hull of an inverted ship. It currently houses the company's Historical Centre.
